opportunities.title: APEX Awards

amount.raw: Applicants can apply for up to £200,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record, holding a permanent or fixed-term position covering the duration of the award, with teaching and admin duties from which they can be relieved, based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Lead applicant may include up to two Co-applicants covering a different Academy remit.
opportunities.summary: Cross-disciplinary seed funding in partnership with the Royal Society and the Royal Academy of Engineering, supported by the Leverhulme Trust, for genuine interdisciplinary and blue-skies curiosity-driven research to benefit wider society, working in collaboration with researchers from other disciplines.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with humanities and social sciences research, working in partnership with a gallery, archive, library or museum (GLAM organisation) or performing arts organisation.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany, with research interest in the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future'.
opportunities.summary: Call for early career scholars in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium (21-23 April 2027) with the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future'. Symposium covers travel, accommodation and visa costs, with seed funding available for collaborations.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: The Academy funds 80 per cent of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC. Three year award.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals eligible regardless of doctorate origin; any nationality with a doctorate from a UK university eligible; others may be accepted with 'strong prior association' with UK. Must have completed Viva Voce between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. Cannot have held a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: Three-year fellowship for an annual cohort of outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards a significant piece of publishable research, funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based HEI or IRO that will continue for the full duration of the award. Independent researchers without institutional affiliation not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Awards to promote acquisition and advancement of skills in core areas (quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, languages) by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination. Funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: up to £300,000 over 2 years (at 80% FEC; total project value at 100% FEC may not exceed £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute with an established role lasting at least the duration of the award, of postdoctoral status or above, spending at least 20% time on the award. Overseas Co-Applicants required; collaboration must be genuinely interdisciplinary and led by and grounded in humanities/social sciences.
opportunities.summary: International interdisciplinary research projects led by UK-based humanities and social sciences researchers with international partners, on the theme of Mobilities, ranging across SHAPE and STEM disciplines. Funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: up to £150,000 for 12 months (with Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Global Innovation Fellowships providing up to two one-year fellowships for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers to embed themselves in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin, developing skills, networks and careers in policy and related sectors.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs

amount.raw: up to £4,000 (exceptional circumstances may consider above £4,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Current British Academy award-holders on any scheme OR applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months who need support submitting an application. Must meet the eligibility requirements of the scheme they intend to apply for.
opportunities.summary: Specific funding to support additional needs of applicants and award-holders (e.g. equipment to overcome barriers for disabled researchers, assistance for sensory impairment, caring costs for research trips, support making applications), considered on a case-by-case basis, in addition to research expenses.
